flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you received feedback you didn’t expect or didn’t fully agree with. What happened next?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q6 Attempt 1]
I'm always open to all feedback, and I always just take note of what that person may be feeling or what I need to be changing, and I try to apply it in the next go-round. I'm always open to everything. Let me see. Let me see. I would say probably during one of my coaching sessions, I had a parent tell me that maybe I should let them kind of more so be free rather than it being so structured. So I took notes from that, and I inserted free play into practices rather than everything being so structured. Pretty well. I feel like they're definitely more comfortable now. Thank you.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time something didn’t go as planned at work and your role in it. How did you handle the responsibility piece?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q7 Attempt 1]
Let's see. I would have to say during an IEP, I was asked what I felt was best for the student. And once I voiced what I felt was best for the student, they kind of went around everything I said and just did what they felt they needed to do. And how I handled that was I just followed their directions, and I just kept suggesting that, well, maybe we should try this, the things that I was suggesting in the meeting. And eventually, once they saw that what they were doing was not working, that's when they decided to give what I was mentioning a shot. I had a student who did not want to sit close to the teacher, and they wanted to sit in the furthest seat away possible. However, the student could not focus, and the parent was not believing that they were going to be able to sit close to the teacher. So I just kept suggesting that the student could not focus. So I just suggested, well, maybe he should sit closer to me. And the parent was just so against it. I'm not sure why. I guess just because the student didn't want to. And they continued on with their normal routine with him, just trying to do like check-ins with me instead of him sitting right in front of me, and it just wasn't working. So I brought up the idea of him sitting closer to me, and they just went for it. And his grades started to soar, and he became more independent, and he was able to ask for help more. It just helped him out a lot more.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Can you share something you’ve learned about children or yourself over time that changed how you approach your work?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q9 Attempt 1]
Um, I would have to say patience. Um, rushing to do anything isn't going to solve anything. Um, being, uh, using your first response to answer to somebody isn't always the best. It's just patience. Take time to breathe. If you're upset, take time to breathe. Um, that's for students and myself as well. If you need time to step away, then do that. Um, communication also, communication is very big. Um, if we just voice how we're feeling to one another, the day can just go along so much smoother.
